text:
Elliot Price: quick IA question for Private backup/restore docs. Where do we want this to live in the public-ish operator docs vs internal Confluence? I’m seeing 3 things: (1) overview + concepts, (2) runbooks (create/verify + restore in-place + restore to new cluster), (3) DR planning (RPO/RTO tiers + game day template).

Kira Thompson: +1, also naming is currently inconsistent across drafts: “Day-2 Ops Toolkit”, “DR Toolkit”, “Backup/Restore”, “Disaster Recovery”. We should pick a canonical phrase and keep “DR” as secondary.

Vivek Kulkarni: from product side: primary entry should be “Backup & Restore (Redwood Private)”. DR planning is a section underneath. “Day-2 ops” can be in the nav label but I’d avoid it as the main H1.

Elliot Price: ok. proposal for nav:
- Deploy > Redwood Private
  - Operations
    - Backup & Restore
    - Disaster Recovery (RPO/RTO + drills)
And inside Backup & Restore page we link to runbooks.

Kira Thompson: works. For the runbooks, do we want them as separate pages or anchored sections on one page? Operators tend to print/save a runbook page.

Diego Santos: separate pages please. also we’ll likely have versioned behavior in `rw-private-dr` CLI; easier to update “Runbook: Create + Verify Backup” without reflowing everything.

Elliot Price: 👍 separate pages it is.

Talia Benson: reminder: Eng Private asked that Confluence remains the “engineering source of truth” during beta, but we still want publishable docs in the docs site for GA. How do we want to link between them?

Elliot Price: I’d prefer: docs site is canonical for operators; Confluence can keep design notes + internal-only troubleshooting. During beta we can add a small “Internal notes / engineering details” link back to Confluence behind VPN.

Vivek Kulkarni: +1. For customers we shouldn’t point to Confluence. Internal-only ok.

Kira Thompson: naming conventions:
- Use “backup” for the artifact and “snapshot” only if it’s storage-backend specific?
- Use “restore drill” for game day.
- Avoid “DR” in headings unless it’s the DR section.

Diego Santos: also “in-place restore” vs “restore to new cluster” are the exact flows we’re building. let’s standardize those phrases.

Elliot Price: agreed. I’ll lock that terminology.

Kira Thompson: screenshots/diagrams: what are we actually able to show?
- CLI examples (ok)
- Helm values snippet (ok)
- Terraform snippets (ok)
- Console screenshots: do we have a “Backup status” view yet or is that just dashboards?

Diego Santos: no Console UI for backups in v1. Observability is via dashboards (Grafana) + alerts. We can include a screenshot of the “Private Backup/Restore” dashboard once observability-pack lands.

Elliot Price: can we get a stable dashboard name + panel list so the screenshot doesn’t go stale?

Diego Santos: dashboard name is planned: “Private DR / Backup & Restore”. Panels: last successful backup age, job success rate, duration p50/p95, restore drill annotations. Sergio is doing it.

Kira Thompson: diagram request: I want a simple architecture diagram that shows:
- k8s CronJob running `rw-private-dr backup create`
- talks to Postgres (dump + WAL archive if enabled)
- reads artifacts (object store buckets / local PV)
- writes encrypted bundle to storage target (S3/minio/NFS)
- plus optional “staging repo” box for air-gapped
Is that accurate?

Diego Santos: yep. also call out that encryption is either SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 (S3 path) or client-side encryption for file bundles in air-gapped. But we should keep the diagram high-level.

Vivek Kulkarni: please include a small callout in the overview: “Redwood does not hold your encryption keys” (customer-owned KMS/HSM). Security will want that.

Elliot Price: noted.

Connor O'Brien: from release eng: we need a crisp doc landing page that release notes can link to when we say “backup required before upgrade”. If the page moves around, pls coordinate before GA.

Elliot Price: yep. I’ll keep the URL stable under /private/operations/backup-restore (or similar). We’ll redirect if needed.

Talia Benson: action items?

Elliot Price: AI from this thread:
1) Docs IA: Private > Operations > Backup & Restore + Disaster Recovery. Separate runbook pages.
2) Terminology: “Backup & Restore”, “in-place restore”, “restore to new cluster”, “restore drill”. Avoid “snapshot” unless backend-specific.
3) Add one high-level architecture diagram (Kira drafting). Diego to sanity check.
4) Add screenshots: Grafana dashboard (once available). For now placeholder callout “see dashboards”.
5) Add a brief security statement re: customer-owned keys + where encryption happens.
I’ll update the draft outline doc today.

Kira Thompson: I’ll start the diagram in slides (simple boxes) + list of screenshots we still need. Will drop a link here.

Diego Santos: I’ll ping Sergio for the dashboard naming + a sample screenshot when the PR is merged.

Vivek Kulkarni: thanks. once you have IA locked, I’ll update the “Day-2 ops toolkit” messaging in the GA checklist to match.

Connor O'Brien: 👍 pls also add a short “Before you begin” section (permissions + maintenance window expectations) so we can point customers there.

Elliot Price: will do. closing the loop when outline updated.
